reason: The broken icy moon fragments and slow rubble seem suited to the goal of following the farther fragments.
expectation: I expect the fragments and slow rubble to gather into a larger aggregate, though their exact outcome is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The moonlets and dust may advance the close-passing moon storyline, but I chose to follow the existing fragments first.

effect: The fragments formed a bound gathering outside the disruptive inner region, so I can follow its next encounter.
reaction: The contrast between the outer region and the close-passing moon is interesting.
reason: I'll follow the outer gathering into its encounter with the crossing stones.
expectation: The stones may break up or crater the gathering, depending on the impact.

alternatives.reason: This could advance the moonlet path, but I want to finish following the outer fragments first.

effect: The outer fragments gathered into a small moon, completing that goal; the close-passing moon remains.
reaction: I expected possible damage, so the stones joining the gathering was a surprise.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the remaining moonlet path.
expectation: The dust may collect on an ice-rich moonlet, producing a larger body.

effect: The moonlet became a loosely bound rubble moon, setting up the remaining encounter.
reaction: Its weak structure makes the approaching impact interesting.
reason: This is the only offered combination and follows the rubble moon toward the remaining goal.
expectation: The head-on impact may break up or redirect the loose moon, though the precise outcome is uncertain.

effect: The impact redirected the surviving rubble moon toward the giant and stripped some material.
reaction: The orbital change was more consequential than simple breakup.
reason: The only offered combination follows the moon's close approach to the giant.
expectation: The giant's tidal forces may pull the loose moon apart, leaving orbiting debris.

effect: The giant's tidal pull broke up the close-passing moon, and its debris formed rings, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The contrast between ring formation close in and moon formation farther out was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the rubble moon into the giant's tidal region was most worthwhile: it explained how the rings formed while the outer moons remained intact.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the loose moon felt like straightforward setup, especially with only one combination offered.

surprise.text: I expected the crossing stones might damage the outer gathering, but they joined it to form a moon.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the single-option steps left little choice.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the giant's rings and moons evolve, although the run of single-option choices makes me less interested in the gameplay itself.
